title: Core Principles of a Balanced Diet
content: Macronutrient Distribution: Target 45-55% complex carbohydrates, 20-30% healthy fats, and 20-25% lean protein. Use the plate method: half filled with non-starchy vegetables, one-quarter with lean protein, and one-quarter with complex carbohydrates. Sample meal structure: Breakfast (Oatmeal with chia seeds & berries OR egg white omelet with spinach & whole-grain toast); Lunch (Grilled chicken breast or tofu with quinoa and mixed greens); Dinner (Baked salmon or lentil curry with steamed broccoli).

title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) Diet Plan
content: Clinical Target: Glycemic index (GI) management and HbA1c optimization. Strategy: High-fiber complex carbohydrates, low glycemic load, and healthy fats to slow glucose absorption. Sample Meals: Breakfast (Steel-cut oats with ground flaxseed and walnuts); Lunch (Spinach salad with grilled chicken breast, avocado, chickpeas, and olive oil vinaigrette); Dinner (Baked cod or tofu with wild rice and roasted asparagus).

title: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Diet Plan
content: Clinical Target: Reducing metabolic waste buildup and protecting Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR). Strategy: Strict restriction of dietary protein, phosphorus, sodium, and potassium. Sample Meals: Breakfast (Cream of wheat with blueberries and white egg omelet); Lunch (Turkey breast sandwich on white bread with cranberry sauce); Dinner (White rice, boiled green beans, and small portion <3oz lean chicken breast).

title: Hypertension & Cardiovascular DASH Framework
content: Clinical Target: Reduction of systolic and diastolic blood pressure, lowering LDL cholesterol. Strategy: High potassium, high magnesium, high calcium, and low sodium (<1500 mg per day). Sample Meals: Breakfast (Low-fat Greek yogurt with sliced bananas and almonds); Lunch (Whole-wheat wrap with tuna salad, spinach, and tomatoes); Dinner (Grilled salmon, quinoa, and steamed broccoli).

title: Highly Processed Foods & Refined Sugars to Avoid
content: Sugar-Sweetened Beverages: Soda, sweetened energy drinks, and commercial fruit juices cause insulin spikes and visceral fat. Refined Carbohydrates: White bread, pastries, sugary cereals stripped of fiber. Trans Fats: Hydrogenated oils in commercial fried foods aggressively raise LDL and lower HDL cholesterol. High Sodium: Canned soups, bacon, deli meats exacerbate hypertension and fluid retention.

title: Absolute Contraindication: MAOI Medication & Tyramine Foods
content: Absolute Contraindication: Avoid aged cheeses, cured meats, red wine, and soy sauce when taking MAOI antidepressant medications. High Tyramine content triggers a severe, life-threatening hypertensive crisis.

title: Absolute Contraindication: Celiac Disease & Gluten
content: Absolute Contraindication: Avoid wheat, barley, rye, and malt. Gluten causes autoimmune destruction of small intestine villi leading to severe malabsorption.

title: Absolute Contraindication: Gout & High Purine Foods
content: Absolute Contraindication: Avoid organ meats, shellfish, beer, and high-fructose corn syrup. High Purine content rapidly elevates serum uric acid, leading to acute joint crystallization and painful gout flare-ups.

title: Absolute Contraindication: GERD & Lower Esophageal Relaxants
content: Absolute Contraindication: Avoid peppermint, chocolate, citrus fruits, and caffeine. These items relax the Lower Esophageal Sphincter (LES), exacerbating acid regurgitation.

title: Relative Contraindication: Statin Therapy & Grapefruit
content: Drug-Nutrient Interaction: Avoid Grapefruit and grapefruit juice when taking statin medications (e.g. Atorvastatin). Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4 intestinal enzymes, dramatically increasing systemic drug concentration and rhabdomyolysis (muscle breakdown) risk.

title: Drug-Nutrient Interaction: Warfarin & Vitamin K Fluctuations
content: Drug-Nutrient Interaction: Maintain consistent daily intake of Vitamin K-dense foods (spinach, kale, collard greens) if taking Warfarin. Drastic fluctuations directly alter anticoagulant efficacy, risking blood clots or internal bleeding.

title: Cardiovascular & Resistance Exercise Guidelines
content: Aerobic Training: 150 minutes of moderate-intensity (50-70% Max HR) or 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity per week. Calculate Max HR = 220 - age. Strength Training: 2 to 3 days per week targeting major muscle groups (2-3 sets of 8-12 reps using compound movements like squats, deadlifts, push-ups, and rows).

title: Osteoporosis & Bone Density Management
content: Frequency: 3 days per week. Moderate to high axial loading weight-bearing aerobic activities (brisk walking, dancing) and resistance training. Absolute Avoidance: Avoid high-impact spinal flexion or deep twisting movements (standard sit-ups, deep twists) to prevent vertebral fractures.

title: Clinical Contraindications to Stop Exercise Immediately
content: Stop Activity Immediately If: Patient experiences acute chest pain/discomfort (angina), sudden disproportionate dyspnea (shortness of breath), dizziness, syncope/fainting, or neuroglycopenia symptoms in diabetics (blood glucose < 70 mg/dL).

title: Circadian Biology & Sleep Optimization
content: Duration: Target 7 to 9 hours of dark-adapted sleep per night to optimize pulsatile Growth Hormone (GH) secretion and regulate cortisol. Sleep deprivation (<6 hours/night) directly impairs insulin sensitivity and upregulates ghrelin (hunger hormone). Eliminate blue light exposure 60 minutes before bed.

title: Clinical Hydration Protocols & Fluid Restrictions
content: Standard Baseline: Fluid Volume (mL) = Body Weight (kg) x 30 to 35 mL. Fluid Restrictive Pathologies: For patients with Advanced Heart Failure (NYHA III/IV) or Anuric/Oliguric Chronic Kidney Disease, daily fluid volumes MUST be strictly capped (1.5 to 2.0 Liters per 24 hours) to prevent pulmonary edema and acute fluid overload.

title: Neuroendocrine Stress Management & HPA-Axis
content: HPA-Axis Regulation: Chronic psychological distress activates the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal axis, maintaining elevated cortisol and abdominal fat storage. Recommendation: Practice Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) or diaphragmatic breathing (6 breaths per minute) to stimulate vagal nerve tone and downregulate sympathetic activity.
